subject.title: WhatsApp: Gemini thinking tags (<think>/<final>) still leak after #6328 fix

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared strict-mode final-boundary recovery in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90924, and should it be extended with WhatsApp/Telegram delivery coverage before this issue is considered fixed?
rationale: This is a security-sensitive sanitizer semantics choice: recovering visible answers from malformed tags can prevent message loss, but the fallback must not expose hidden reasoning in any channel.

options.title: Adopt Shared Final-Boundary Recovery
options.body: Land or adapt the open shared sanitizer fix and require focused WhatsApp plus sibling-channel regression proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Require A Stream Coordinator Instead
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose a stream-level reasoning lane parser that prevents malformed tagged text from reaching delivery sanitizers.

options.title: Defer Until Live Repro
options.body: Keep current behavior and wait for a current-main live WhatsApp/Gemini reproduction before changing strict sanitizer semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Final-Boundary Recovery
recommendation.body: Land or adapt the open shared sanitizer fix and require focused WhatsApp plus sibling-channel regression proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about shared sanitizer/security semantics, and steipete has the strongest history signal across reasoning/final-tag sanitizer and provider-reasoning behavior.
